methods.name: Agent-behaviour evaluation
methods.definition: Drive a real agent through a scenario and score the transcript against the criterion, for a requirement whose subject is an agent's behaviour.

methods.name: Architecture conformance
methods.definition: Check the implemented dependency structure against the declared one, so a layering rule is enforced rather than documented.

methods.name: Spec-by-example (BDD)
methods.definition: Execute the worked examples the requirement was specified with, so the example and the test are one artifact.

methods.name: Combinatorial t-way testing
methods.definition: Cover every t-way combination of declared configuration dimensions, rather than every combination or one arbitrary combination.

methods.name: Compile-time check
methods.definition: Encode the property so that violating it does not compile — a lint promoted to a hard error, a type that cannot represent the bad state, a const assertion. The evidence is that the build succeeded, and there is no runtime cost or runtime escape.

methods.name: Concolic / symbolic execution
methods.definition: Explore execution paths symbolically to find inputs that reach a state, rather than sampling inputs and hoping one does. An escalation: reach for it after cheaper search has stalled, not first.

methods.name: Consumer-driven contract testing
methods.definition: Assert that a provider's output satisfies the schema its consumers were written against, checked from both sides independently.

methods.name: Dynamic application security testing
methods.definition: Probe the running system's exposed surface for exploitable behaviour, from outside, without its source.

methods.name: Demonstration
methods.definition: The system is operated in front of a witness and observed to do the thing. Produces no source symbol.

methods.name: Design by contract
methods.definition: Encode preconditions, postconditions and invariants as executable annotations on the implementation, checked wherever it runs.

methods.name: Deterministic simulation
methods.definition: Run the system under a seeded, controlled scheduler so a concurrency failure reproduces exactly rather than intermittently.

methods.name: Dynamic analysis (sanitizers)
methods.definition: Run the program under an instrumented runtime that reports undefined behaviour, data races, leaks or use-after-free the source does not show and no assertion would catch. Distinct from fuzzing, which generates the inputs, and from static analysis, which never executes.

methods.name: End-to-end testing
methods.definition: Drive the assembled system through the interface a user or caller uses.

methods.name: Fault injection
methods.definition: Induce a failure the system claims to tolerate — a dropped connection, a full disk, a killed process — and observe that it does.

methods.name: Formal analysis (SMT)
methods.definition: Encode the requirement set as constraints and ask a solver about consistency, redundancy, gaps, or a witness for a claim.

methods.name: Fuzzing
methods.definition: Execute the input surface against generated or mutated data, looking for crashes, hangs and assertion failures rather than wrong answers.

methods.name: Golden / approval testing
methods.definition: Compare output byte-for-byte against a reviewed, checked-in artifact, so an unintended change is a diff rather than a surprise.

methods.name: Grammar-based fuzzing
methods.definition: Fuzz with inputs generated from a grammar, so the generated data reaches past the parser into the logic behind it.

methods.name: Interactive application security testing
methods.definition: Observe the running system from inside during exercise, correlating requests with the code paths they reach.

methods.name: Inspection
methods.definition: A person reads the artifact against the requirement and records a verdict. Produces no source symbol, so it is discharged through the inspections registry rather than by a tagged test.

methods.name: Integration testing
methods.definition: Exercise two or more components across their real boundary, without substituting the boundary itself.

methods.name: Metamorphic testing
methods.definition: Assert a relation between the outputs of two related executions, for a requirement whose correct output cannot be stated independently.

methods.name: Model-based test generation
methods.definition: Derive test cases from a state or protocol model rather than authoring them, so the generated set covers the model's transitions.

methods.name: Temporal model checking
methods.definition: Exhaustively check a temporal property against a state model, returning a counterexample trace rather than a pass.

methods.name: Mutation testing
methods.definition: Seed faults into the implementation and measure whether the existing suite detects them — a test of the tests, not of the code.

methods.name: Negative / abuse-case testing
methods.definition: Exercise the paths an adversary or a mistaken caller takes, asserting the system refuses rather than that it succeeds.

methods.name: Performance benchmarking
methods.definition: Measure a quantified metric against its declared target and threshold — the NFR measurement row, executed.

methods.name: Property-based testing
methods.definition: Execute a property over generated inputs, asserting an invariant that holds for every input rather than a fixed expected value.

methods.name: Runtime verification / monitors
methods.definition: Check a temporal property continuously against a running system, for a requirement no single execution can discharge.

methods.name: Static application security testing
methods.definition: Match declared rules against source to find a defect class without executing it.

methods.name: Software composition analysis / SBOM
methods.definition: Enumerate dependencies and check them against known-vulnerability and licence policy.

methods.name: Static quality analysis (ISO 5055)
methods.definition: Measure structural quality weaknesses — complexity, coupling, known defect patterns — over the source.

methods.name: Unit testing
methods.definition: Exercise one unit in isolation against a fixed expected result.
